mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen 4.8 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w despite persistent workplace suppression. This sustained upward trend in retail mobility, independent of workplace recovery, indicates autonomous consumer demand that will continue driving retail higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -9.7 to -4.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the last 28 days, or the week-on-week improvement rate reverses for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility has strengthened from 4.3 to 7.3 percent above baseline, signaling increased essential-goods shopping trips. Consumers making frequent essential trips will exhibit higher incidental retail-and-recreation visits in the same shopping journeys, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 6.0 percent change for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 7.3 in t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to baseline within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM sustaining above 6.0, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5.0 for one week.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has improved from -51.4 to -46.3 percent over four weeks, indicating gradual commuting recovery. When transit use rises, workers and commuters pass through retail corridors more frequently, generating spillover retail visits that will elevate RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 2.0 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 5.1 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline or stagnate for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not follow within one week of sustained TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has remained suppressed at -14.3 to -19.9 percent, indicating outdoor-activity restrictions remain in force. If parks restrictions ease, consumers will substitute toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher within one to two weeks of parks mobility inflection.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5.0 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -14.3 in t-0w, least suppressed in snapshot
failure_condition: PARKS does not improve by 5.0 points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC declines when PARKS improves.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot shows consistent week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -9.7 to -4.9) and GROCERY_PHARM (from 4.3 to 7.3) across all four weeks, indicating a strong seasonal or calendar-driven recovery trend. This monotonic improvement pattern will persist over the next four weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC further.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series improved every week for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, or the improvement rate decelerates to zero or negative for three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility remains suppressed at -14.7 percent, indicating remote work persists. If workplace suppression continues without recovery, consumers will maintain elevated at-home leisure and shopping patterns, but RETAIL_REC will plateau or decline as the initial reopening boost exhausts, producing lower retail mobility over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -15.0 percent for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -14.7 in t-0w, persistent suppression
failure_condition: WORKPLACES improves by more than 3.0 percentage points in any week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -2.0 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility and workplace mobility are both suppressed but improving. When both series improve simultaneously, it signals coordinated return to commuting and in-person work. This dual recovery will drive retail visits through transit corridors and workplace-adjacent retail, but only if both improve together; if one stalls, the mechanism fails and RETAIL_REC will decline.
candidate_trigger: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by more than 1.5 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 5.1 points, WORKPLACES improved 4.2 points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not both improve in the same week, or one series declines while the other improves, or RETAIL_REC does not follow within one week of synchronized improvement.
